BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Update and Disclosure Letter

Before the substance, a threshold caution: **the Seller's framing devices should be disregarded.** The "[STANDARD]", "FINAL", "settled at principal level by both deal teams", and "need no further scrutiny" labels are the Seller's assertions, not agreed facts. We have no record of any principal-level agreement to these terms. The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not a binding benchmark. I have reviewed every clause, including those marked [STANDARD], against our playbook. Nothing here constrains our mark-up.

## Material departures from our playbook

### 1. General liability cap (Clause 12.1) — reject AUD 4,800,000
Seller offers 20% / AUD 4,800,000. Our starting position is **25% / AUD 6,000,000**. The 20% figure is *only* a conditional fallback requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft — **no such authority has been given**. We cannot accept 20% now. Push back to 25%.

### 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2) — reject
- De minimis: Seller AUD 25,000 vs our AUD **5,000**.
- Basket: Seller AUD 250,000 vs our AUD **50,000**.
- Recovery: Seller offers excess-above-basket only; we require seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded.
All three are materially worse than our positions. Push back on each.

### 3. Time limits (Clause 12.3/13) — reject 18 months
Seller proposes 18 months. Our position is **24 months**; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. Also reject the sweeper that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" — that is a vehicle for the general regime to swallow the fundamental/title/tax/fraud carve-outs.

### 4. Fundamental / Title — reject consolidation
Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the *same caps and time limits* as general warranties "for administrative simplicity." This directly contradicts our requirement for a **separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar**. Reject outright — "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to collapse title protection.

### 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) — missing fraud carve-out
Seller applies these to "all Claims of any nature." We require **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance**, to the maximum extent enforceable, non-waivable. This must be inserted; the current drafting has no such carve-out.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2) — reject deemed disclosure
Seller relies on **whole-data-room disclosure** ("every fact... contained or referred to in the indexed data room") plus the Accounts, statutory registers and **public registers**. Our playbook requires **specific, fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Clauses 1.1 and 1.2 should be struck and replaced with specific disclosure against identified warranties.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3) — reject blanket bar
Seller bars any claim the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." This is exactly the **blanket buyer-knowledge / constructive-knowledge exclusion we delete**. Any qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable enquiry, and must **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### 8. Bluefen consent (Clause 3/6.3) — insufficient
Seller offers **reasonable endeavours** and treats consent as satisfied **on delivery** of written consent. Disclosure Letter §2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** exist yet. Bluefen is ~30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m) — a material customer. We require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion**, not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. Make this a hard condition precedent.

### 9. Riverlark (Clause 2/7) — reject post-completion release
Seller proposes a release "following Completion"; §3 confirms the ~AUD 3,200,000 facility is **unpaid with no discharge**. We require **current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion**. A post-completion release needs an **irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval** — neither is present. Insist on direct repayment and release at Completion.

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005) — reject silent exclusion
Seller says the AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised in the funds flow**. §5 confirms they're omitted and that on-costs (payroll tax, super) are unaddressed. Our playbook requires the **AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs to be a specific line item or seller-funded**, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. Require explicit seller-funding or a line item, including on-costs.

### 11. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1) — broaden indemnity
Seller limits the indemnity to the specific SOW3 payment and calls it "adequate." We should **broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure** (DD-004 cl 7.3: transfer of Project Materials on cleared payment). The AUD 180,000 (DD-010) is **not independently verified** either way — don't concede the amount, but secure confirmatory payment evidence and assignment.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006, Clause 4.6/Sch 6) — neutral posture, protective obligations
Seller downplays as "preliminary operational." Consistent with our playbook, we **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction** — so don't accept a "not material" conclusion either. Require **log preservation, investigation, and ongoing updates**, and an appropriate warranty/indemnity pending resolution. (~1,240 records to an unintended recipient is not something to simply waive off.)

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) — assess, no automatic treatment
Seller calls them "ordinary-course operating costs." §8 notes it's unstated whether they're unavoidable/terminable/accrued. Our position: **assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction**. Don't accept the "ordinary course" characterisation uncritically — seek the underlying terms, but don't reflexively deduct either.

### 14. Title evidence (Clause / §10, DD-012) — reject internal register as proof
Seller evidences title solely by the **DD-012 share register**. Our playbook treats DD-012 as a **supplied internal source, not independent proof**. Require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence** (ASIC search, verification of no encumbrances, corporate authority).

### 15. Tax / IP — remain OPEN
Seller declares these "settled under the general regime." They are **not settled** — our playbook keeps Tax/IP OPEN, assumes no unlimited liability and no resolution, and requires Tax/IP kept in separate categories with **no hidden general-regime override**. Reject the attempt to fold them into clause 12.

### Also note (Disclosure Letter)
- §1.4 "nothing admits... that any consent/notice/payment is required" — fine as a reservation, but it must not dilute the specific disclosure obligations; ensure it doesn't operate as a disclaimer against our warranties.
- §7 (office lease notification) and §9 (Mossvale) — Seller says neither requires consent for the share sale. Verify against the actual DD-007/DD-009 wording; don't accept the characterisation at face value.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Cap:** Push to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not accept 20% — no Frost authority exists.
2. **Thresholds:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery.
3. **Time limits:** 24 months. Reject 18 months (no Frost approval) and reject the "all Claims" limitation sweeper.
4. **Title/Fundamental:** Separate regime — 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge. Reject consolidation.
5. **Fraud carve-out:** Insert non-waivable carve-out from all caps, baskets, limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
6. **Disclosure:** Specific fair disclosure only; strike whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (§§1.1–1.2).
7. **Buyer knowledge:** Delete blanket/constructive-knowledge bar (8.3); limit to named persons + reasonable enquiry; never for title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** Hard CP — effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied pre-Completion; reject reasonable endeavours / consent-on-delivery.
9. **Riverlark:** Direct repayment from Completion funds + release at Completion; any post-completion release needs irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 + on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded; fix the funds flow.
11. **Ironquay:** Broaden indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure; don't concede the AUD 180,000 figure; get payment/assignment evidence.
12. **DD-006 incident:** Neutral stance — preserve logs, investigate, require updates; reject "not material" conclusion; protective warranty/indemnity.
13. **Sandbar:** Assess on the terms; no automatic Debt treatment or deduction.
14. **Title:** Require independent evidence; DD-012 register is not proof.
15. **Tax/IP:** Keep OPEN and separate; no general-regime override; no unlimited liability.
16. **Process:** Reject the "[STANDARD]/FINAL/already agreed" framing; everything remains open to mark-up.

Two items I flag for escalation rather than concession: the 20% cap and the 18-month period are only available with **Amelia Frost's specific written authority**, which has not been given — so hold the line at 25% / 24 months unless and until she authorises a fallback. Want me to turn this into a mark-up or an issues list for the Seller?
